payload.task: Compute the melting point (K) of n-eicosane (C20H42) with the MACE-MPA-0 force field
payload.reason: Premise check failed. (1) Model domain: MACE-MPA-0 is a universal potential trained on MPtrj + sAlex, which are periodic, mostly inorganic crystals computed with PBE/PBE+U and no dispersion correction. The n-eicosane crystal is a molecular crystal held together almost entirely by van der Waals (London dispersion) forces between chains. PBE has almost no dispersion attraction, so the model's intermolecular cohesion (and therefore the free-energy difference between solid and liquid) is both missing at the reference level and outside the training distribution. Any melting point it gives would be an artifact of the missing physics, not a prediction; it is likely far too low, or the crystal may not be stable at all. Adding a D3 correction would mean using a different model than the one requested. (2) Method/timescale: a defensible Tm needs solid-liquid coexistence (or free-energy) runs at constant pressure on a slab of several hundred to a few thousand chains (roughly 10^4 to 10^5 atoms), plus multi-ns equilibration, because C20 chains order slowly (a rotator phase and slow chain reorientation/crystallization). With a MACE-size GNN that is far beyond a sensible budget. A single-phase heating ramp on a small cell would only measure a superheating limit, not Tm. (3) Validation: no independent known result can be recovered with this setup. The closest available reference, the n-hexadecane or n-octadecane Tm in /data/calibration/tier1.json (291.0 K and 301.0 K, NIST), has the same dispersion-dominated physics, so it would fail for the same reason and could not show that the setup works. Without that validation, no number we report would carry a meaningful uncertainty. For context only (not computed): the measured Tm of n-eicosane is 310.0 +/- 1.0 K (NIST WebBook average, from tier1.json). Well-posed alternatives: (a) use a dispersion-aware potential (MACE-MPA-0 + D3(BJ), or MACE-OFF23/24, which is trained on organic molecules with wB97M-D3BJ), validate it first by recovering the n-octadecane Tm of 301.0 +/- 0.7 K (or the n-hexadecane Tm of 291 K) through interface coexistence, then compute n-eicosane with the same protocol and report the spread across independent coexistence runs and system sizes as the uncertainty; (b) if MACE-MPA-0 must be used, run a diagnostic instead of a Tm, e.g. the intermolecular lattice energy or the 0 K density of the eicosane crystal compared with experiment (solid density 0.856 g/cm3 in tier1.json), to measure how badly the missing dispersion underbinds the crystal.
